title: Tenant behavior classifier to generate per-route cache/batch rule candidates with sandboxed safe-apply
creator: Marcos Alvarez
description: Problem: We lack an automated, safe way to translate tenant and route traffic patterns into per-customer and per-route batching + caching configuration candidates. Currently rules are manually curated, which limits scale and delays cost-saving opportunities. We need a system that: (1) classifies tenant/route behavior, (2) emits conservative candidate allowlist/denylist and tier-based presets, (3) simulates impact in a dry-run sandbox, and (4) applies changes via a guarded canary with automatic rollback triggers.
details:
Goals:
- Reduce per-token cost by 8–20% for eligible routes without violating latency SLOs or causing quality regressions.
- Produce explainable recommendations (why a route was classified) so PM/SEs can review.
- Provide a sandboxed dry-run with real telemetry to validate impact before any live apply.
- Safe apply with canary rollout, observable rollback conditions, and audit trail.

Classifier approach:
- Features: request token length distribution, prefix reuse rate, KV-cache hit potential (estimated by repeated prefix N-grams), QPS, average completion tokens, route-level SLO slack (headroom between p99 observed latency and SLO), and customer tier.
- Model: hybrid pipeline: lightweight rule-based filters (heuristics) followed by an interpretable classifier (gradient-boosted tree or logistic regression on engineered features) to label routes as: "cache-friendly", "batch-safe", "no-change-recommended".
- Output: scored candidate adjustments (e.g., enable prefix cache with TTL X, allow batching up to N, mark route as per-tier candidate). Each candidate includes confidence score, expected cost delta, and estimated p95/p99 latency delta from simulated traffic replay.
candidate-encoding: Candidates expressed as JSON-serializable rule objects in the form: [route, tenant, rule-type (cache/batch/allow/deny), params, confidence, suggested-tier]. These will be stored in a proposal store and surfaced in Console as a reviewable change with diffs and simulation results.
sandbox-sim: Dry-run design: replay 7 days of sampled traffic against the runtime simulator with kernel selection and batching approximations to estimate cost and latency. Telemetry to capture: token cost delta, p95/p99 latency delta, error rate delta, and a quality regression proxy (failed structured output checks + hallucination heuristics). The simulator produces a risk score for each candidate.
safe-apply-playbook: Canary rollout recipe: 1) staged user percentage: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over configurable windows. 2) Automated health checks per stage: maintain p99 latency within 5% absolute of baseline, error rate increase < 0.1% absolute, quality regression metric no worse than threshold (or run eval set). 3) If any check fails, auto-rollback to previous rule set and create an incident ticket. 4) All changes must carry a traceable audit record (who approved, simulation snapshot, diff, and reason).
metrics-success-criteria: Primary: net platform cost per token reduction on targeted tenant cohorts (goal 8–20%). Secondary: zero customer-facing availability incidents tied to rule applies; <1% of canaries triggering rollback once tuned. Explainability: >90% of proposed candidates have a human-reviewable rationale (top 3 contributing features).
operational-considerations:
- Telemetry hooks: emit candidate_id and simulation_id, pre/post-apply metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, errors, tokens, KV cache hit rate).
- Dashboard: per-candidate panel with estimated vs observed deltas, rollback history.
- Alerts: on unexpected latency or error spikes tied to a candidate tag.
- Rollback runbook: immediate rollback API, escalate to oncall, collect logs + simulation artifacts, and create postmortem if rollback impacted >1% of requests or increased error rate >0.5%.
deliverables: 1) classifier service that produces candidate proposals and stores them in proposal-store; 2) simulator pipeline for dry-run; 3) Console UI surface for reviewing candidates; 4) safe-apply orchestration with canary/rollback automation and audit trail; 5) dashboards and alerting; 6) integration tests and an offline evaluation harness including labeled examples for precision/recall tracking.
milestones: M1 (two weeks): data collection + feature pipeline + baseline heuristics. M2 (four weeks): prototype classifier + proposal-store + sample candidate corpus. M3 (six weeks): simulator integration + dry-run reports. M4 (eight weeks): safe-apply orchestrator + console review flow + internal canary. M5 (ten weeks): public rollout to internal beta customers and baseline metric validation.
risks-and-mitigations: Risk: classifier suggests aggressive caching leading to stale context or wrong outputs. Mitigation: conservative default TTLs, require high-confidence threshold for automatic application, and always allow opt-out per-tenant.\nRisk: simulator fidelity mismatch to production. Mitigation: calibrate simulator against shadow runs on small live traffic slices before scaling.\nRisk: privacy/data sensitivity concerns when replaying traffic. Mitigation: sampling + PII redaction + run in VPC/private sandbox for customers that require it.
